program_name: Intelligent Mechatronics Engineering (Master's degree). This is the renewed 2026/27 name of the former Master's Degree in 'Mechatronics Engineering' / 'Ingegneria Meccatronica'. The 2026/2027 non-European admission call was still issued under the previous name 'Mechatronics Engineering (classe LM-33 R)', and UniTrento states that applicants selected under that call are automatically admitted to the new Intelligent Mechatronics Engineering degree; the official non-EU ranking published in May 2026 is already titled 'Master in Intelligent Mechatronics Engineering'.
teaching_language: Fully English. The official course sheet states 'LANGUAGE: English' with no Italian parallel track and no Italian percorso: the whole two-year, 120-ECTS programme is delivered in English ('All the courses are taught in English'). This is a stand-alone English-taught Master's degree (one of the UniTrento 'Master's degrees in English' that use the dedicated non-EU tuition/scholarship scheme), not an English pathway inside an Italian-taught degree. No Italian language requirement is set for admission or graduation in the sources consulted.
campus: Trento - Povo campus. Department of Industrial Engineering (DII), 'Ferrari 2' Building, Via Sommarive 9, 38123 Povo, Trento (TN). Lessons take place only in person; admitted students must be in Trento for the start of classes.
degree_class: LM-33 (R) - Ingegneria meccanica / Mechanical Engineering. The corsi.unitn.it course sheet states 'CLASS TYPE: LM-33 - Mechanical engineering' and the 2026/27 admission call states 'Mechatronics Engineering (classe LM-33 R)'. Note that orienta.unitn.it labels the same code as 'LM33 - Ingegneria industriale', which is a legacy/incorrect label for the class name (the code LM-33 itself is consistent across all sources).
admission_type: Two separate procedures. (1) EUROPEAN AND EQUIVALENT CANDIDATES: open / free access ('ACCESS: Free'; 'The programme is free access to Europeans and Equivalents') with mandatory verification of curricular, personal-background and language requirements - no numero programmato, no entrance ranking, no TOLC/SAT. Every applicant must still submit an online admission request, including students already enrolled at UniTrento and those who already meet all requirements. (2) NON-EUROPEAN CANDIDATES RESIDING OUTSIDE ITALY: restricted access through a dedicated selection call (Call for Applications for admission to the Master's Degree Programs of the Department of Industrial Engineering, A.Y. 2026/2027) with 25 reserved places, merit-based evaluation of the academic curriculum and a published ranking.
application_deadline_eu: A.y. 2026/2027 - European and equivalent candidates (this category also includes non-EU citizens permanently residing in Italy with a valid stay permit for study, long-term residence, employment, family, asylum, subsidiary protection or religious reasons, and non-EU citizens permanently resident in Italy who obtained their secondary school diploma in Italy): admission request open from 18 May 2026 to 12 November 2026. Applications may be submitted before graduating or before all curricular requirements are met; the outcome is communicated by email within one month of submission (rolling evaluation). Bachelor's degree must be obtained by 31 October 2026 for Europeans and equivalents (and for non-Europeans graduating in Italy with a valid study permit).
application_deadline_non_eu: A.y. 2026/2027 - non-European candidates residing outside Italy: single deadline, application by 4 March 2026 at 12:00 CET (application fee EUR 30, to be paid by the same deadline; non-payment means exclusion). Ranking published on the programme page by 20 May 2026 (the actual ranking PDF for Intelligent Mechatronics Engineering was published on 13 May 2026). Confirmation of the place plus the EUR 100 enrollment confirmation fee within the deadline stated in / communicated with the ranking. Pre-enrolment on Universitaly within 2 weeks from confirmation, then study visa at the Italian embassy/consulate. Bachelor's degree must be obtained by 30 June 2026 for non-Europeans graduating outside Italy. Visa must be obtained no later than 31 October 2026 and all international students must arrive in Trento by 31 October 2026.
entry_exam_or_test: No standardised entrance exam (no TOLC, no GRE/GMAT, no SAT) and no numero programmato test for either category. (1) EU and equivalent candidates: document-based verification of the curricular requirements (ECTS per scientific disciplinary sector, SSD). For candidates with a degree obtained abroad and recognised as eligible, 'the verification of the adequacy of the personal background may also include a test before a committee appointed by the Departmental Council'. An optional, non-mandatory, anonymous online self-assessment test on mechanics, physics, electronics, automation and IT is offered on the Prerequisites page (Google Form), together with video tutorials; it has no effect on admission. (2) Non-EU candidates: no written test - a Selection Committee of at least three faculty members (appointed by Rectoral Decree) evaluates the application dossier and awards up to 100 points; 'In the event that the documentation attached to the online application does not allow the Committee to adequately assess the candidacy, the applicant may be required to attend an interview.' The Committee may meet online. (3) Applicants of either category who cannot document English B2 must sit and pass the English proficiency test at the UniTrento Centro Linguistico di Ateneo (CLA) before enrolment (written part in person in Trento, speaking part online).
academic_requirements: EUROPEAN AND EQUIVALENT CANDIDATES (free access, requirement verification): a Bachelor's degree or equivalent university qualification of at least three years' duration, also obtained abroad if recognised as suitable. Curricular requirements by background: (a) Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, class L-9, from the University of Trento - curricular requirements automatically met; (b) Bachelor's degree in class L-9 from another Italian university - at least 18 ECTS in the SSD IMIS-01/A (ex ING-IND/12 Mechanical and Thermal Measurements), IIND-02/A (ex ING-IND/13 Applied Mechanics), IIND-03/A (ex ING-IND/14 Mechanical Design and Machine Construction), IINF-01/A (ex ING-INF/01 Electronics), IINF-04/A (ex ING-INF/04 Systems and Control Engineering), MATH-04/A (ex MAT/07 Mathematical Physics); (c) Bachelor's degree in a different class - at least 54 ECTS distributed across three groups, all three of which must be satisfied: at least 24 ECTS in MATH-02/A (ex MAT/02 Algebra), MATH-02/B (ex MAT/03 Geometry), MATH-03/A (ex MAT/05 Mathematical Analysis), MATH-03/B (ex MAT/06 Probability and Mathematical Statistics), MATH-05/A (ex MAT/08 Numerical Analysis), STAT-04/A (ex SECS-S/06); at least 15 ECTS in PHYS-01/A (ex FIS/01), PHYS-02/A (ex FIS/02), PHYS-03/A (ex FIS/03), CHEM-03/A (ex CHIM/03), CHEM-05/A (ex CHIM/06), CHEM-06/A (ex CHIM/07); at least 15 ECTS in IMIS-01/A (ex ING-IND/12), IIND-02/A (ex ING-IND/13), IIND-03/A (ex ING-IND/14), IINF-01/A (ex ING-INF/01), INFO-01/A (ex INF/01 Informatics), IINF-04/A (ex ING-INF/04), IMIS-01/B (ex ING-INF/07 Electric and Electronic Measurements), MATH-04/A (ex MAT/07). For a degree obtained outside Italy, requirements are assessed by a Committee appointed by the Departmental Council based on content equivalences with the SSD listed above, and the adequacy of the personal background may additionally be checked by a test before that Committee. No GPA threshold and no seat cap is published for this category. NON-EUROPEAN CANDIDATES RESIDING OUTSIDE ITALY (selection call, a.y. 2026/2027): 25 reserved places for this Master's degree (the same quota of 25 applies to each of the four DII English-taught Master's degrees; the Mechatronics quota includes applicants selected within the EIT Digital and SPECTRO programmes). Requirements: a Bachelor's degree of at least 3 years obtained or to be obtained by 30 June 2026, in Industrial Engineering (Italian class L-9) or in any Industrial Engineering discipline (Mechanical, Mechatronics, Chemical, Materials Engineering) or Electronic Engineering discipline (Electronic, Control, Automation Engineering), or any Industrial Engineering-related field awarded by an internationally recognised university, with a study plan proving basic knowledge and competencies in Mathematics and Physics; AND a weighted average mark of passed exams (excluding the final project) of at least 23/30, or the equivalent GPA in the country of graduation. Selection: the Committee awards a maximum of 100 points - coherence between previous studies and the objectives of the Master's degree (max 30 points), curriculum studiorum, i.e. marks and results in previous studies, post-graduate courses and extra-academic activities (max 60 points), additional language skills, i.e. English above B2 or other languages (max 10 points). Candidates scoring at least 50/100 are eligible/admitted; ties are broken in favour of the youngest candidate. Applicants who did not pay the EUR 30 fee or do not meet the entry requirements are declared ineligible. Candidates may apply to more than one DII Master's degree but must submit a separate application (and fee) for each. SCHOLARSHIPS AND FEES (non-EU only): 2 scholarships were available for a.y. 2026/2027 in this programme, awarded from the top of the ranking to candidates scoring at least 70/100 - no separate scholarship application is needed; a scholarship holder is exempt from tuition fees and receives a partial contribution to mobility expenses paid after arrival in Italy (not compatible with MAECI, Unicolor or Invest Your Talent in Italy scholarships). Maximum tuition for non-EU citizens living abroad is EUR 6,000 per year, reduced by admission score: 90-100/100 tuition waiver; 70-89.99 EUR 1,000; 60-69.99 EUR 2,000; 50-59.99 EUR 4,500. In the second year, students who paid fees in the first year are fully exempted if they earn at least 42 ECTS by 10 August 2027 (42+ waiver; 36-41 EUR 1,000; 24-35 EUR 2,000; 6-23 EUR 4,500; under 6 EUR 6,000). Non-EU students admitted to a programme are entitled to guaranteed on-campus accommodation (paying rent). Degrees obtained abroad are verified only after admission and pre-enrolment; UniTrento may request a CIMEA/ENIC-NARIC statement of verification and/or comparability. [uncertain] Two clauses of the DII call appear to be copy-paste artefacts from the DISI call: it refers to qualifications 'awarded abroad in the field of Information Engineering and Computer Science' and states that the Selection Committee is chosen 'from among the teaching staff of the Department of Information Engineering and Computer Science (DISI)', whereas the programme belongs to the Department of Industrial Engineering (DII) and the course page describes the eligible fields as Industrial and Electronic Engineering.
language_requirements: English at CEFR level B2 (all four skills) is required; no Italian language requirement is set. EUROPEAN AND EQUIVALENT CANDIDATES may prove it either (a) by having passed a university exam in English at B2 level as part of their degree programme, or (b) by providing a language certificate recognised by UniTrento (list published by the Centro Linguistico di Ateneo, CLA, at cla.unitn.it/node/780). Applicants holding neither can take and pass the CLA English test before enrolment; once the requirement is met they must email the Student Support Service to proceed with enrolment. The written part is held in person in Trento at the CLA and the speaking part online. Six sessions are scheduled for admission to Master's degrees in 2026: Session 1 - registration 27 March to 20 April 12:00 CET, written 27 April 14:30, speaking 8 May; Session 2 - registration 20 April to 15 May 12:00, written 25 May 14:30, speaking 5 June; Session 3 - registration 16 May to 25 June 12:00, written 6 July 14:30, speaking 17 July; Session 4 - registration 26 June to 21 August 12:00, written 2 September 14:30, speaking 11 September; Session 5 - registration 24 August to 2 October 12:00, written 12 October 14:30, speaking 23 October; Session 6 - registration 5 October to 13 November 12:00, written 23 November 14:30, speaking 4 December. Registration is via a dedicated online form (webapps.unitn.it/Apply/en/Web/GoHome/ammissione/ENAdm_STA26). NON-EUROPEAN CANDIDATES must document B2 by the application deadline of 4 March 2026 through one of: an international English certificate; a B2-or-higher English exam passed at another university (level and all four skills must be tested and certified); a Bachelor's degree run entirely in English (to be certified - a written statement from the university that English is the official teaching language of the degree is accepted); citizenship of a country whose official language is English (self-declaration; a self-declaration of having graduated in an English-speaking country is also accepted on the course page). English proficiency above B2 and knowledge of other languages earn up to 10 additional points in the non-EU merit ranking.
required_documents: NON-EUROPEAN CANDIDATES (online application via the dedicated procedure, EUR 30 fee): (1) a copy of a valid passport - only the pages with photo and personal data; (2) a copy of the Bachelor's degree certificate if already awarded, or a certificate of enrollment stating the expected graduation date (full information on the grading scale is mandatory, otherwise the application is not considered); (3) a transcript of academic records listing all courses, exams, marks awarded, the weighted average mark and the minimum-to-maximum range of marks - undergraduate candidates must also list exams not yet passed; (4) curriculum vitae et studiorum in English, preferably in Europass format; (5) proof of English proficiency at B2 as described in the language requirements. An official translation into English (or Italian) is required for any document not originally in English or Italian; illegible documents are not considered and incomplete or non-submitted forms are excluded. Graduates of an Italian university submit a self-declaration under DPR 445/2000 instead of the degree certificate and transcript; UniTrento students/graduates do not upload these documents at all. Later stages: EUR 100 confirmation fee, pre-registration on Universitaly (Step 6 of 'First steps') and study-visa application at the Italian consulate/embassy - an admission letter is issued only after Universitaly pre-registration is completed; a CIMEA/ENIC-NARIC statement of verification and/or comparability may be requested. EUROPEAN AND EQUIVALENT CANDIDATES (online admission request on the UniTrento portal, webapps.unitn.it/Apply, section 'ammdii26'; authentication with SPID or CIE for Italians aged 18+, or a guest.unitn.it account for foreigners/those without Italian ID): applicants who are studying or have studied at another university must attach a self-declaration of the exams taken, stating for each exam the Scientific Disciplinary Sector (SSD), the credits (CFU), the date it was taken, the final grade and the syllabus (detailed course programme), plus documentation of English B2 where available. All applicants must apply, including those already enrolled at UniTrento and those who already meet every requirement.

uncertainty_notes: 1) PROGRAMME RENAMING / ACCREDITATION: for a.y. 2026/2027 the former 'Mechatronics Engineering' (Ingegneria Meccatronica) was restructured and renamed 'Intelligent Mechatronics Engineering'. The non-EU admission call published in December 2025 still uses the old name and class label 'Mechatronics Engineering (classe LM-33 R)', and corsi.unitn.it warns that the 2026/2027 educational offer 'may undergo some changes until the final accreditation of the course by the MUR, expected in June 2026'. The renaming is confirmed as effective by the non-EU ranking PDF published on 13 May 2026, which is titled 'Master in Intelligent Mechatronics Engineering'. UniTrento variously writes 'Intelligent Mechatronic Engineering' (singular, on the legacy page) and 'Intelligent Mechatronics Engineering' (on the new course site, the manifesto and the ranking); the latter is the form used on the official course page and is treated as the official name here. 2) CALL TEXT INCONSISTENCIES: the English courtesy translation of the DII call is explicitly non-binding ('The only legally binding version of the call is the Italian one. This is a courtesy translation produced with the support of AI-assisted tools') and contains two apparent copy-paste errors from the DISI call - it accepts foreign qualifications 'in the field of Information Engineering and Computer Science' and states that the Selection Committee is drawn from the staff of DISI, whereas this is a DII programme whose course page describes the eligible fields as Industrial and Electronic Engineering. These points should be confirmed with stem.admissions.int@unitn.it. 3) SECOND-YEAR CURRICULA: the four new curricula (Mechanics; Robotics and Intelligent Vehicles; Space Systems and Instruments; Electronics and Smart Energy Systems) replace the previous tracks (Mechanics; Electronics and Robotics; Intelligent Vehicles) still listed on orienta.unitn.it. The manifesto marks the second year as 'INACTIVE A.A. 2026/27' because students enrolling in 2026/27 reach it only in 2027/28 - this is normal and does not indicate a suspended curriculum. 4) DEGREE CLASS LABEL: corsi.unitn.it and the call give LM-33 (R) with the correct class name 'Mechanical engineering / Ingegneria meccanica'; orienta.unitn.it mislabels the same code as 'Ingegneria industriale'. The code LM-33 is consistent everywhere. 5) NO INTERATENEO OR DOUBLE-DEGREE REQUIREMENT: a testimonial on the course page mentions a 'Double Degree Program' with Germany for the former Mechatronics Engineering degree, but no double/joint degree agreement, partner university or dedicated admission route is declared in the 2026/27 admission sources consulted; double-degree participation is not an admission requirement. 6) EU/EQUIVALENT DEADLINE: 18 May - 12 November 2026 is stated on the programme's own EU admission page (last published 14 May 2026); no earlier or later session and no application fee is mentioned for this category, but the admission request must be submitted through the shared DII procedure 'ammdii26' on webapps.unitn.it/Apply, which is login-gated and could not be inspected without UniTrento credentials, so the live portal wording could not be cross-checked. 7) SOURCE ACCESS: corsi.unitn.it and www.unitn.it are behind an AWS WAF 'Human Verification' layer that returned HTTP 405 to direct fetching; all corsi.unitn.it pages and PDFs cited above were retrieved through a plain-text reader proxy of the same official URLs and cross-checked against orienta.unitn.it (directly reachable) and search-engine results. All figures come from the official 2026/27 pages, call and ranking. 8) NO ITALIAN LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT is mentioned anywhere for this programme, unlike some UniTrento English-taught bachelor tracks; no Italian proficiency test appears in the deadlines for either candidate category.
